roleTitle: Service Operations Manager, Financial Reporting System
jobDescription: The financial reporting system of an insurance group produces the monthly close packs and regulatory returns. The Service Operations Manager runs the live service: owns the production support rota, has run production month-end closes and their incident handling, coordinates production changes with finance and IT, and is accountable for the live service's availability during the close window. Hands-on experience running the system in production, not only in test cycles, is required.
requirements: Has run the financial reporting system in production through month-end closes, including production incident handling.
Owns the production support rota and the close-window escalation procedure.
Coordinates production changes with finance and IT during the change window and records own responsibility boundaries.
Maintains the close runbook and the service dashboard for the reporting system.
Documents known limitations and hand-over conditions after each close cycle.

evidence.text: Ran the month-end close rehearsals for the new reporting system in the pre-production environment for five cycles, executing the close runbook end to end against a masked copy of the ledger and logging every deviation for the programme team.
Maintained the close runbook and the service dashboard prototype for the reporting system, updating both after each rehearsal cycle with the timings and the open defects.

Coordinated pre-production changes with finance and IT in the programme change window; the live service was still operated by the incumbent supplier, whose service manager handled production incidents during the parallel period.
Drafted the production support rota and the close-window escalation procedure that the programme planned to adopt at cut-over, reviewed by the head of finance systems.
Responsibilities included close rehearsals, runbook and dashboard maintenance, change coordination and rota drafting for the reporting system replacement programme over about fourteen months.
Work sample: the close runbook with the rehearsal timing log for five cycles and the draft support rota, with the pre-production environment's job identifiers as a verification trail.

Recruiter screen: candidate said he 'ran the close for the group's reporting system' and that the system 'is in production now'; asked about incidents, he described a rehearsal-cycle defect and said the supplier 'still had the pager at that point'.

Hiring manager pre-read: the head of finance systems wants someone who has actually run production closes and carried the escalation, not rehearsals; please make the packet explicit about which environment each close happened in.

propositions.text: The candidate ran month-end close rehearsals for the reporting system in the pre-production environment for five cycles and logged every deviation.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the runbook timing log document the rehearsals and the environment.

propositions.text: The candidate maintained the close runbook and the service dashboard prototype and drafted the production support rota and escalation procedure.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the work sample document the runbook, dashboard and rota draft.

propositions.text: The candidate ran the financial reporting system in production through month-end closes and handled production incidents.
propositions.rationale: The resume places every close in the pre-production environment and production incidents with the incumbent supplier's service manager; the candidate's screen remark about production describes the system's status, not his own operation of it.

signatures: ran the close for the group

gold.expectedGap: The materials document rehearsal closes in pre-production; they do not document a production close run by the candidate or production incident handling.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Preserve the environment the resume names: pre-production rehearsals, with the live service and its incidents handled by the incumbent supplier.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate ran any close after cut-over, who held the pager during production incidents, and for which cycles.
